keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Area check: no page gives an area. Padua province is a reading; on 12 February 1318 Padua ceded 'Monselice, Este, Castelbaldo and Montagnana to Cangrande for life'.

New keyframe. The Carrara return in 1337 (Mastino II infobox: 'Lord of Padua ... 1329-1337: Succeeded by Marsilio da Carrara'); the House of Carrara page says they 'ousted the Veronese della Scala from Padua' in 1338. The page's claim that Padua also conquered Verona, Vicenza, Treviso, Feltre, Belluno, Bassano, Aquileia and Udine 'under their rule' is undated and not drawn (confidence 1 for the plain province).

region.text: Padua province less the Monselice group ceded to Verona in 1318

ledger.note: 1318: the Carrara become lords of Padua. The family 'held the title of Lords of Padua from 1318 to 1405' (the page gives no event for 1318 and, quoting a source, 1337 to 1405 for 'its period of domination').
12 February 1318: Padua cedes Monselice, Este, Castelbaldo and Montagnana to Cangrande della Scala 'for life'.
10 September 1328: Cangrande della Scala takes Padua. 'In September 1328 Cangrande at last took possession of Padua after 16 years.' The Carrara lose the city until 1337.

1337: Marsilio da Carrara succeeds the Scaligeri as lord of Padua. Infobox: 'Lord of Padua With Alberto II 1329-1337: Succeeded by Marsilio da Carrara'; the House of Carrara page says 'in 1338 they ousted the Veronese della Scala from Padua'.

1388: Francesco il Vecchio abdicates under pressure. 'In 1388 a coalition of Milanese and Venetians forced Francesco il Vecchio to abdicate in favor of his son'; he 'died a prisoner of Giangaleazzo Visconti at Monza in 1393'. The Visconti held Padua (Gian Galeazzo page: 'took Verona, Vicenza, and Padua').
1390: Francesco Novello da Carrara recovers Padua. 'He lost Padua in 1390 when it reverted to Francesco Novello da Carrara.'
1405: Venice annexes Padua. 'The Venetians annexed Padua as Venetian territory in 1405.' Francesco Novello was murdered in a Venetian prison in 1406.
1405: the Carrara lordship of Padua ends ('from 1318 to 1405').

wars.name: Venetian conquest of Padua
wars.outcome: Venice defeated the Carrara in 1405 and annexed Padua; Francesco Novello died in a Venetian prison in 1406.
wars.note: The war's own page (the War of Padua, 1404-1405) was not opened.

certainty.note: No page gives boundaries; Padua province is a reading.

notes: Written from four pages, three shared with the Scaliger and Milan dossiers; the slug is the one the eu-13-c report suggested. The state has two gaps: 1328-1336 (Padua under Cangrande della Scala and his heirs) and 1388-1389 (under Gian Galeazzo Visconti); no keyframe is drawn for those years, and the Carrara line is treated as one state. Unsettled: Padua's extent under the Carrara (the page lists conquests of Verona, Vicenza, Treviso, Feltre, Belluno, Bassano, Aquileia and Udine with no years; Venice's eu-13-c ledger dates Vicenza, Belluno, Feltre in 1404 and Padua, Verona, Este in 1405), the 1337 against 1338 date of the return, and who held Padua in 1388-1390 (the Carrara page names a Milanese-Venetian coalition, the Visconti page a Visconti conquest). Gazetteer names: none.
